summary: Check and repair managed background services during node up, including already-ready nodes
details: Background up validates both generated systemd units, migrates the recognized pre-console controller template, installs a missing console observer and verifies its running state before reporting success. A ready core also starts the independent private console without restarting Bitcoin, balance-history, the indexer or the chain.

Observer units carry a release identity so an upgraded node kit reloads long-running monitor code. Repeated up calls leave a current healthy observer running. Installed controller timeout and image-pull settings are preserved; existing disabled autostart remains disabled, and a newly installed observer inherits the controller boot policy.

Custom units, unsupported template changes, drop-ins, masks and unreliable systemd observations require explicit operator review. Permission or startup failure returns a nonzero result instead of treating core READY as complete background startup.

Foreground mode and dry runs do not install systemd services. A node without a bootstrap controller still requires explicit controller install or foreground operation. Release activation remains explicit.
operator_actions: Follow the normal release upgrade procedure and run usdb-node up. Use the node operator account and provide sudo credentials when service installation or startup requires them. Review any reported custom systemd configuration before replacing it.
